html:
The Charka, or Charcas, were an Aymara-speaking people and lordship of the highlands of northern Potosí, in central Bolivia. After the fall of Tiwanaku around 1000 to 1100, the high Andes split into rival lordships, the Aymara kingdoms.

The Charka formed a confederation with their neighbours the Qhara Qhara and other groups. When the Inca took the region in the later 1400s, the Charka became valued soldiers of the empire, guarding the eastern frontier against the Chiriguano. In 1582 their lords joined in writing the Memorial de Charcas, reminding the Spanish crown of that service. The Spanish gave their name to the Audiencia of Charcas, the high court in La Plata (now Sucre) that governed the land that became Bolivia. Their country lay close to the silver of Potosí.
